key_insight: FiLIP learns CT representations from report-derived abnormal findings, avoiding the assumption that different patients’ scans should always have dissimilar embeddings.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support CT finding classification and radiology report generation, but clinical utility remains to be established.
method: Use a large language model to extract abnormal finding phrases from radiology reports.
Convert the findings into semantic target features using a biomedical text embedding model.
Train the CT image encoder to predict these findings-aware features.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved multi-label zero-shot finding classification over weakly supervised approaches in both in-domain and external-domain evaluations, plus benefits for report generation after fine-tuning.
watch_item: The abstract provides no dataset sizes or numerical performance gains, limiting assessment of the magnitude and robustness of the improvements.
paper_title: Findings-aware Language-Image Pretraining for CT Volume Interpretation
